text:
cara: heads-up — onboarded a customer and their quickstart hit two weird parity issues that feel SDK-specific. Posting repros.

lin: pls paste repros, thx.

cara: 1) response headers: when calling generate via curl the server returns x-rate-limit-remaining and x-model-variant headers we use to backoff and pick evals. Our Node SDK strips those headers from responses so sampleapp sees none and keeps hammering the API and also runs the wrong eval set. curl: `curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $T' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` -> headers present. SDK: `await client.generate({prompt:'hi'})` -> response body only, no headers.

lin: wow — did SDK intentionally hide headers or did middleware drop them?

cara: I inspected the http client wrapper — it maps `response.data` directly and discards `response.headers`. That was probably to simplify the high-level API but it's breaking ops and onboarding. We need to surface response metadata at least behind a `meta` field or provide an option to request raw response.

lin: agreed. what's the second issue?

cara: 2) client-side batching: the SDK introduced an "auto-batcher" for small gen requests to improve throughput. It merges requests issued within 5ms into one batch POST. For most workloads that's fine, but our quickstart does two back-to-back prompts expecting independent completions and ends up with the server receiving a single concatenated prompt -> model output mixes both contexts and the UI displays garbage. Repro: sampleapp calls `client.generate({prompt:'Q1'})` then immediately `client.generate({prompt:'Q2'})` and gets a single completion for `Q1\nQ2`. curl sequential calls work fine.

ops-bot: alert: this batching behavior has caused 3 customer incidents this week (tickets #3241, #3242, #3243).

lin: sounds like two fixes: (A) expose response headers in the SDK response shape (e.g., `{data, meta:{headers}}`) and document which headers clients should rely on, (B) make auto-batching opt-in or require explicit `batchable:true` flag, and avoid merging if requests have differing user-provided metadata (e.g., request_id, conversation_id). Also add a short debounce threshold increase and a per-request opt-out.

cara: +1. Also request: when surfacing headers, include a convenience accessor for x-rate-limit-* and x-model-variant so sampleapps don't have to parse raw headers. For the batching, let's default to conservative (no batching) for quickstart builds; we can enable aggressive batching in high-throughput examples.

lin: I'll open DX-700 for header surfacing + helper fields and DX-701 for batching changes. For immediate mitigation, add a patch to quickstart to insert a 20ms await between sequential generate calls and a note in docs about batching being enabled in some SDK builds.

devex-bot: jira:DX-700 created by lin - "SDK: surface response headers (x-rate-limit-*, x-model-variant) in response.meta and provide helpers"

devex-bot: jira:DX-701 created by lin - "SDK: make auto-batching opt-in and respect per-request metadata; default to conservative in quickstart builds"

cara: thanks — applying the 20ms pause unblocked the onboarding for the customer. Will rerun with SDK patch once DX-701 lands. :thumbsup:
